第一章 语音
第一部分：语音
共5个小题，每小题1分，共5分。要求从所给的四个单词的划线部分中选出一个与其他三个读音不同的选项。
音节
音节是语音的最小单位，可由元音音素单独构成，也可由元音音素加辅音音素构成，还可由辅音音素中的响音/n/和/l/独自构成（即无须与元音音素结合）。
英语的单词可仅包含一个音节，称为单音节词，如：fame/feɪm/；也可包含两个或多个音节，称为双音节词或多音节词，如：famous/ˈfeɪməs/和famously/ˈfeɪməslɪ/。
两个元音音素之间有一个辅音音素时，辅音音素归后一音节；有两个辅音音素时，一个辅音音素归前一音节，一个归后一音节。
重读音节
在双音节词或多音节词中，读得特别响的那个音节叫重读音节，其他为非重读音节（多音节词有时还可有一个次重读音节）。单音节词本身就是重读音节。
重读音节中的元音字母后若没有辅音字母（如：no），或虽有辅音字母（r除外）但后跟一个不发音的字母e（如：note），则称为重读开音节；重读音节中的元音字母后若有辅音字母（r除外）且其后没有不发音的字母e（如：not），则称为重读闭音节。

lessons.title: 代词
lessons.src: 成人高考（高起点）-第二章-词汇与语法-代词.doc

blocks.s: 代词是用来代替名词短语以避免重复的一种词性。
Mr. Li ate the tofu.
He liked it.
主格与宾格
He called at nine o’clock yesterday.
He loves me and is proud of me.
—Who’s that knocking at the door?
—Me.
物主代词
Your performance is better than mine.
My performance, however, is much better than his.
反身代词
（1）反身代词作宾语
I consider myself an honest man.
The manager gave himself a raise.
I watched the cat giving itself a bath.
反身代词作宾语，必须等同原句中的主语，指同一人或同一物。
（2）反身代词作同位语
Study itself is not so enjoyable.
I didn’t like the pearl itself, but the box was quite elegant.
反身代词作同位语，不一定是指主语，可以和主语不同。
代词常见错误
代词有且只有一个先行词。
代词与先行词的一致性。
代词与谓语动词的一致性。
代词有且只有一个先行词
Although the new regulations allow people to do ________, people seldom go out.
When students first found this website, the teachers thought ________ were very lucky people.
代词与先行词的一致性
（一）人称
In the cafe, customers will enjoy ________ in the pleasant environment.
（二）单复数
The cats are hungry. Can you feed ________?
（三）性别
If a student passes ________ exam, ________ teacher will be pround of ________.
代词与谓语动词的一致性
代词作主语时的主谓一致。
He has two children. ________ loves ________ very much, and ________ love ________ dearly, too.
重难点总结
代词有且只有一个先行词。
代词与先行词的一致性：人称、单复数、性别。
代词与谓语动词的一致性：主谓一致。

lessons.title: 副词
lessons.src: 成人高考（高起点）-第二章-词汇与语法-副词.doc

items: 副词通常用来修饰动词、形容词或副词，但有几类副词也可以修饰名词。
（1）修饰语和它所修饰的对象应尽量接近。
（2）修饰语应避免有两个以上可能修饰的对象。

blocks.s: （1）表示方法状态的副词，用于修饰动作“是怎么做的”，所以是修饰动词专用的修饰语。
[1] I waited for my wife. [patiently]
[2] He stayed single. [reluctantly]
[3] He greeted the girl. [warmly]
He greeted the girl standing by the bar.
[4] He asked the girl a question. [politely]
[5] The girl considered herself an attractive woman. [proudly]
修饰动词专用的副词
（2）表示频率的副词，有always, frequently, usually, often, seldom, hardly, never等，用于修饰动作发生的频率，是修饰动词专用的副词。
[1] I get up very early. [usually]
[2] I have seen this teacher before. [never]
修饰四大词性的副词
（1）强调范围的副词，用于将叙述范围缩小到明确的焦点上，排除其他可能性，也可以说是“聚焦”的功能。
[1] I watched the video yesterday. [only]
修饰四大词性的副词
（2）加强语气的副词，和强调范围的副词一样，也是修饰的对象不拘，四大词性都可以使用，所以它的位置也没有任何弹性，只能放在修饰对象的前面。
[1] The teacher is absolutely a genius!
[2] I badly need to take this course.
[3] The course is extremely useful.
[4] My English improves amazingly fast.
修饰四大词性的副词
（3）程度副词，又是一种修饰对象不拘、四大词性都可以使用的副词 。所以，它的位置同样没有弹性，只能放在修饰对象的前面。
[1] I barely need to take this course.
[2] The course is fairly useful.
[3] My English improves rather fast.
连接句子的副词
连接句子的副词的意思和并列连词(and, or, but)类似，但是缺乏并列连词的语法功能。也就是说，虽然连接句子的副词可以用来表示前后两个从句之间的逻辑关系，但是不能用它来连接两个从句，因为它没有连词的功能。若要用连接句子的副词连接两个从句，必须加上适当的标点符号，例如用分号把两个从句分开，或者用句号断开变成两句话。
连接句子的副词
[1] I know this teacher; besides, the course is extremely useful. (and)
[2] Consequently, I badly need to take this course. (so)
[3] He is short; however, he plays basketball well. (but)
分离副词
这类副词原本属于另一个从句，是该从句中的一个方法状态副词。
[1] Theoretically, the course should be useful.
[2] Theoretically speaking, the course should be useful.
[3] If we are speaking theoretically, the course should be useful.
介副词
所谓介副词，就是一些看起来像介词，后面却不加宾语、直接拿来当副词使用的词。
[1] The screen is on.
[2] Sit down please.
[3] Turn on the screen please.
时间副词与地点副词
[1] The football game tomorrow is going to be exciting.
[2] All the people here are my students.
[3] I had lunch there yesterday.
[4] The football game is tomorrow.
[5] The detective is here. Something's up.

lessons.src: 成人高考（高起点）-第二章-词汇与语法-名词短语.doc

blocks.s: 本节课适合的人群 1. 名词单复数经常用错 2. 冠词经常用错
通过本节课，你可以 1. 掌握名词的数 2. 掌握不定冠词、定冠词和零冠词
名词短语=限定词+形容词+名词
可数名词
英语句子中的单数可数名词，在前面限定词的位置要么用冠词a/an来表示“一个”，如：a computer，an apple；要么用其它的限定词，如：my computer，the apple。
英语句子中的复数可数名词，在词尾加上 –s（或其它不规则的复数变化）来表示“两个及以上”，在前面限定词的位置可以用零冠词，如：computers, apples；也可以用a/an以外的一些限定词，如：my computers, the apples。
不可数名词
英语句子中的不可数名词，在前面限定词的位置可以用零冠词，如：money, water；也可以用a/an以外的一些限定词，如：my money, the water。
可数名词/不可数名词
名词短语的省略
（1）形容词

items: 复数可数名词或不可数名词，可以用零冠词。
在语意清楚的情况下，可以省略名词。

blocks.s: Of these answers, this one is the best.

The new is not always better than the old.

名词与限定词的一致性
名词与前面的限定词在可数、不可数方面必须一致
a large number of
a large amount of
数字的写法
three thousand computers
thousands of computers
冠词
She spent ________ hour waiting in the queue. That was ________ long hour indeed.
She ordered ________ new French-English dictionary. ________ dictionary was published in France.
In ________ spring ________ weather gets warmer, but in ________ spring of 1942 it was very cold.
This is too expensive; do you have ________ cheaper room?
I’ll take ________ cheaper of the two rooms.
专有名词
（1）普通名词代表的是“通称”的概念：同一个名词，可以有两个以上的对象通用。
person, place
（2）专有名词代表的是“特称”的概念：一个名词只适用于单一的对象。
Li Haogang, America
假专有名词
America / the US
the Himalayas
the Atlantic
专有名词普通化
You are not ________ Li Haogang I know.
普通名词专有化
（1）只设一席的职称
They elected his father ________ chairman of the committee.
（2）同位语
Lionel Messi, ________ captain of Barcelona, is a skilful player.
普通名词抽象化
I never go to ________ hospital, but often go to ________ hospital to visit my aunt these days.
He seldom went by ________ bus, so she was surprised when seeing him on ________ bus.
重难点总结
英文句子中的名词必须是名词短语的结构，尤其是一定要有限定词（包括零冠词）。
定冠词the的重点在于“指示性”，零冠词的重点则在于“不加限定/无限”。
构成名词短语的三个部分，只要符合条件、语意清楚，分别都有可能被省略。

lessons.title: 动词的时态
lessons.src: 成人高考（专升本）-第二章 动词的时态.doc

blocks.s: 动词主要知识点
时态和语态
分词视为形容词
过去分词(done)如果前面加上助动词have，写成have done，这种构造是完成式。
除此之外，分词可以当做形容词看待。
在分析句型时，视be动词为动词，后面的分词短语为形容词补语，那么就只剩下一般式与完成式这两种状态。
一般式
一般式的情况通常就是这样：说出一段时间，动作只要落在这段时间之内就行。
一般式状态可以用图像的方式来理解：在时间线上，用一个括弧标示出时间范围，动作就发生在这个范围中。前、后括弧表示是有开始、结束的一段明确时间，范围可大可小。
一般过去时
I ________ (see) Mr. Li last week.
一般过去时的被动语态
When I was young, we ________ (teach) to treat older people with respect.
过去进行时
I ________ (record) an online course when the power suddenly went out.
I ________ (record) an online course throughout last week.
过去进行时的被动语态
The house ________ (build) when it collapsed.

blocks.s: 动词主要知识点
分词视为形容词
过去分词(done)如果前面加上助动词have，写成have done，这种构造是完成式。
除此之外，分词可以当做形容词看待。
基本句型的被动语态
所谓被动语态的句子，可以这样来理解：把句中的宾语拿出来当主语，句子就要改写为被动语态。

items: 在五种基本句型中，下列三种使用及物动词的句型有包含宾语在内：
主语+谓语动词+间接宾语+直接宾语
主语+谓语动词+宾语+宾语补足语

blocks.s: 主语+谓语动词+宾语

Zhi Zunbao gave Zi Xia a hug.
主语+谓语动词+宾语+宾语补足语
Zhi Zunbao called Sun Wukong a dog.
完成式的被动语态
Because he ________ (leave) the textbook in the classroom, Mr. Li came back soon.
进行式的被动语态
I ________ (record) an online course now.
表示人的感觉
The test results are satisfying to the student.
The student is satisfied with the test results.
The student considers the test results satisfying.
被动语态的使用原则
以英文的使用习惯而言，一般都是使用主动语态，因为主动语态比较简洁（通常比被动语态少几个字），也比较清楚、直接。
如果采用被动语态能够加强句子的连贯性、清楚性或者简洁性，才应该采用被动，否则应一律使用主动语态。

The textbook had been left in the classroom by him.
清楚性
They/People ________ (speak) English in England.
简洁性
Because Mr. Li urged him to study hard, the student found a book and started to read.

blocks.s: 形容词和副词都有比较级与最高级的变化。只要是以连词as或than连接的比较级句子，都可以视为主句加从句所构成的主从复合句结构。而这里的从句，就是从属连词as或than引导的状语从句。
比较级的从句虽然是状语从句，但是因为英文的比较句法具有平行对称的要求，所以有许多特色都和并列复合句相似。除了平行对称，比较句法也和并列复合句一样经常会有省略的情形。这是因为，两个符合平行对称要求的分句往往会有重复的部分，而重复会影响简洁性，因此要设法省略。
不过，比较句法虽然近似并列复合句，但是比较级的句子毕竟还是从句中的状语从句类，所以有些变化仍然和并列复合句不尽相同。例如比较句法经常可以选择用倒装句来表示，这就和一般的并列复合句不一样。

blocks.s: 1. ag, act to do or drive 做；驱使
四级词汇

agent /ˈeɪdʒənt/ [ag=to do 做；-ent n.=person 人→“person who does 办事者”→] n. ① a person or company that represents another person or company, especially in business {Our agent in Rio deals with all our Brazilian business.} ② someone who finds work for actors, musicians etc, or who finds someone to publish a writer’s work {My agent has a new script for me to look at.}
四级词汇

agency /ˈeɪdʒənsi/ [ag=to do 做；-ency n.=the quality or state 表性质或状态→“the abiliy or place of doing business 办事的能力或场所”→] n. ① a business that provides a particular service for people or organizations {a local housing agency} ② an organization or department, especially within a government, that does a specific job {a UN agency responsible for helping refugees}
四级词汇
agenda /əˈdʒendə/ [ag=to do 做；-enda（-a表复数）n.=things 事情→“things to be done 要办的事项”→] n. a list of the subjects to be discussed at a meeting {the next item (=subject) on the agenda}
四级词汇

act /ækt/ [act=to do 做→“to do what is required 做要求的事”→] v. ① to do something in a particular way or for a particular reason {The company acted correctly in sacking him.} ② to perform in a play or film {I first started acting when I was 12 years old.} n. a law that has been officially accepted by Parliament or Congress {the Housing and Community Development Act of 1977}
▽actor [act; -or n.] n. 男演员；行动者
actress [act(o)r; -ess n.] n. 女演员
四级词汇

action /ˈækʃən/ [act=to do 做；-ion n.=process or result of 表过程或结果→] n. the process of doing something, especially in order to achieve a particular thing {The government must take action (=do something) now to stop the rise in violent crime.}
四级词汇
active /ˈæktɪv/ [act=to do 做；-ive a.=able to ~ 会……的→] adj. always busy doing things, especially physical or mental activities {She’s over 80, but is still very active.}
▽activate* [activ(e); -ate v.] v. 使活动
activist [activ(e); -ist n.] n. 活动分子，积极分子
activity [activ(e); -ity n.] n. 能动性；活跃；[复] 活动
四级词汇
actual /ˈæktʃuəl/ [act=to do 做；-u-；-al adj.=the act or fact of 表行为或事实→] adj. used to emphasize that something is real or exact {I’m not joking. Those were his actual words.}
四级词汇
exact /ɪɡˈzækt/ [ex-=out 出；act=to drive 驱使→“to drive out；driven out 逼出来；逼出来的”→] adj. completely correct in every detail {Police are still investigating the exact cause of the accident.}
四级词汇
react /riˈækt/ [re-=back 回返；act=to do 做→] v. to behave in a particular way or show a particular emotion because of something that has happened or been said {How did Wilson react to your idea?}
▽reaction [react; -ion n.] n. 反应；反作用；反动
四级词汇

interact /ˌɪntərˈækt/ [inter-=between 在…之间；act=to do 做→“to do between two things 在两者之间互动”→] v. ① if people interact with each other, they talk to each other, work together etc {Lucy interacts well with other children in the class.} ② if one thing interacts with another, or if they interact, they affect each other {The immune system interacts with both the nervous system and the hormones.}
▽interaction [interact; -ion n.] n. 相互作用；相互
interactive [interact; -ive a.] a. 互相作用的；[计] 交互的
四级词汇
transact /trænˈzækt/ [trans-=across or through 穿过；act=to drive 驱使→“to drive through 使通过”→] v. to do business with someone {Most deals are transacted over the phone.}
▽transaction [transact; -ion n.] n. 办理，处理；交易，业务

四级词汇

deceive [de-=away 离；ceive=to take 取→“to take sb away from (what is true) 带某人离开（真相）”→] v. to make someone believe something that is not true {He had been deceived by a young man claiming to be the son of a millionaire.}

perceive /pəˈsiːv/ [per-=thoroughly 完全地；ceive=to take or grasp 握住→“to grasp thoroughly 完全掌握”→] v. ① to understand or think of something or someone in a particular way {Often what is perceived to be aggression is simply fear.} ② to notice, see, or recognize something {Cats are not able to perceive colour.}
▽perception [per-; cept; -ion n.] n. 感知，感觉；察觉

accept /əkˈsept/ [ac-(ad-)=to 到；cept=to take 取→“to take (sth offered) to oneself 将（他人给的东西）取到自己手中”→] v. to take something that someone offers you, or to agree to do something that someone asks you to do {Rick accepted her offer of coffee.}

except /ɪkˈsept/ [ex-=out 出；cept=to take 取→“to take out 取出”→] prep. used to introduce the only person, thing, action, fact, or situation about which a statement is not true {The office is open every day except Sundays.} v. to not include something {High technology equipment would be excepted from any trade agreement.}
▽exception [except v.; -ion n.] n. 除外，例外；异议，反对

anticipate /ænˈtɪsəpeɪt/ [anti-(ante-)=before 前；cip=to take 取；-ate v.→“to take before or realize before 先取得，先实现”→] v. ① to expect that something will happen and be ready for it {Sales are better than anticipated.} ② to do something before someone else {When Scott reached the South Pole he found that Amundsen had anticipated him.}
▽anticipation [anticipat(e); -ion n.] n. 期望；预期；先发制人

principal /ˈprɪnsəpəl/ [prin=first 首位；cip=to take 取；-al adj.=of …的→“of taking first 占取首位的”→] adj. most important {Teaching is her principal source of income.} n. ① someone who is in charge of a school {a small school with just three teachers and the principal} ② the main person in a business or organization, who can make important business decisions and is legally responsible for them {The principal of the business has an office in New York.}

process /ˈprəʊses/ [pro-=forward 向前；cess=to go→going 行走→“going forward 前进运动”→] n. ① a series of actions that are done in order to achieve a particular result {Repetition can help the learning process.} ② a series of things that happen naturally and result in gradual change {Coal forms by a slow process of chemical change.}

decide /dɪˈsaɪd/ [de-=away 离；cid=to cut 切；-e →“to cut away 切掉”→“to cut short and bring an end to sth 切断某事使之告结”→] v. ① to make a choice or judgment about something, especially after considering all the possibilities or arguments {You must decide for yourself.} ② to make an official or legal judgment {The Commission will have the power to decide disputes.}

decision /dɪˈsɪʒən/ [decide的对应名词：de-=away 离；cis=to cut 切；-ion n.=the act or result 表行为结果→] n. a choice or judgment that you make after a period of discussion or thought {Do you ever wonder if you made the right decision?}

precise /prɪˈsaɪs/ [pre-=beforehand 事先；cis=to cut 切；-e →“cutting off (vagueness) beforehand（含糊的东西）事先已切除的”→] adj. ① precise information, details etc are exact, clear, and correct {It was difficult to get precise information.} ② used to emphasize that you are referring to an exact thing {The precise cause of the disease is unknown.}

claim [claim=to call out 呼喊→“to speak loudly (for one's own rights)（为自身权益）呼喊”→] v. to state that something is true, even though it has not been proved {The product claims that it can make you thin without dieting.} n. a statement that something is true, even though it has not been proved {They made claims they couldn’t live up to.}

exclaim /ɪkˈskleɪm/ [ex-=out 出；claim=to call or shout 喊→“to call or shout out 喊出来”→] v. to say something suddenly and loudly because you are surprised, angry, or excited {‘No!’ she exclaimed in shock.}

blocks.s: 16. clin, clim to lean or slope 倾斜
四级词汇

incline /ɪnˈklaɪn/ [in-=towards 向；clin=to lean 倾斜；-e →“to lean towards 向…倾斜”→] v. ① if a situation, fact etc inclines you to do or think something, it influences you towards a particular action or opinion {The accident inclined him to reconsider his career.} ② to slope at a particular angle, or to make something do this {The telescope is inclined at an angle of 43 degrees.} n. a slope {a steep incline}

四级词汇

decline /dɪˈklaɪn/ [de-=down 向下；clin=to lean 倾斜；-e →“to slope down 向下倾斜”→] n. a decrease in the quality, quantity, or importance of something {There has been a decline in the size of families.} v. ① to decrease in quantity or importance {Car sales have declined by a quarter.} ② to say no politely when someone invites you somewhere, offers you something, or wants you to do something {The court declined to review her case.}
四级词汇

clinic /ˈklɪnɪk/ [clin=to lean 倾靠；-ic n.=a place 场所→“a place for sick persons to lean back or a place with sick-beds 让病人可以倚靠的场所，或有病床的场所”→] n. a place, often in a hospital, where medical treatment is given to people who do not need to stay in the hospital {women attending an antenatal clinic}
▽clinical [clinic; -al a.] a. 临床的；疾病的
四级词汇

climax /ˈklaɪmæks/ [clim=to lean 倾斜；-ax n.=things 表事物→“things which lean for going up 用于登高的倾斜的工具”→“ladder for reaching a goal at a high place 用于探取高处目标的梯子”→] n. the most exciting or important part of a story or experience, which usually comes near the end {the climax of his naval career} v. if a situation, process, or story climaxes, it reaches its most important or exciting part {a series of special events climaxing with a spectacular fireworks show}
四级词汇

climate /ˈklaɪmət/ [clim=to lean or slope 倾斜；-ate n.=the state 表状态→“the state of sloping surface of the earth toward the sun 地面对于太阳倾斜的状态”→“the state of a certain region on the earth influenced by the sun 地球上某地区受太阳影响的状态”→] n. the typical weather conditions in a particular area {Los Angeles’ warm dry climate}
▽climatic [climat(e); -ic a.] a. 气候的

amateur /ˈæmətə/ [amat=to love; -eur (-er) n.=person 人→“persaon who does sth for loving it (rather than for money) 因爱好（而不是金钱）从事某项活动者”→] n. ① someone who does an activity just for pleasure, not as their job {Mickelson won his first major golf tournament while still an amateur.} ② someone who you think is not very skilled at something {You English are a bunch of amateurs when it comes to romance.}

animal /ˈænəməl/ [anim=life生命；-al n.=thing characterized by 具有…特征的东西→“thing characterized by having life 有生命的东西”→] n. ① a living creature such as a dog or cat, that is not an insect, plant, bird, fish, or person {The cosmetics have not been tested on animals.} ② any living creature that is not a plant or a person {He can’t stand cruelty to animals of any sort.} ③ any living creature, including people {Man is a highly intelligent animal.}

animate /ˈænɪmeɪt/ [anim=life 生命；-ate adj.=having 有…的→“having life or spirits 有生命的，有精神的”→] v. to give life or energy to something {Laughter animated his face for a moment.} adj. living {animate beings}

anniversary /ˌænəˈvɜːsəri/ [anni=year 年；vers=to turn 转；-ary n.=thing 物→“the day connected with the turning of a year 与时间周转一年相关的日子”→] n. a date on which something special or important happened in a previous year {Jack and Kim celebrated their twentieth wedding anniversary in January.}
四级词汇

annual /ˈænjuəl/ [annu=year 年；-u-；-al adj.=of …的→] adj. ① happening once a year {The school trip has become an annual event.} ② based on or calculated over a period of one year {a household with an annual income of $60,000}

audience /ˈɔːdiəns/ [aud=to hear 听；-i-；-ence n.=the act or state 表行为或状态→“the act or state of hearing 听的行为或状态”→] n. a group of people who come to watch and listen to someone speaking or performing in public {The audience began clapping and cheering.}
四级词汇

auditorium /ˌɔːdəˈtɔːriəm/ [audit=to hear 听；-orium n.=place 场所→“place for hearing 听的场所”→] n. ① the part of a theatre where people sit when watching a play, concert etc ② a large building used for concerts or public meetings

audio /ˈɔːdiəʊ/ [audi=to hear 听；-o adj.=of …的→“of hearing 与听有关的”→] adj. relating to sound that is recorded or broadcast {audio and video equipment} n. the part of a recording that contains sounds and music but not pictures {You can save the audio for editing later.}

august /ɔːˈɡʌst/ [aug=to increase 使增大；-ust adj.=the most 最→“to increase to the most 增到最大”→“the greatest 最伟大的”→] adj. impressive and respected {an august institution}
August /ˈɔːɡəst/ n. ① 奥古斯特（即古罗马凯撒大帝Augustus，他自认为是最伟大的帝王）② 八月（奥古斯特大帝以自己的名字命名八月份）
四级词汇

author /ˈɔːθə/ [auth（auct）=to cause to grow 使成长；-or n.=person 人→“person who causes anything to grow 使事物产生者”→] n. ① someone who has written a book {He was the author of two books on China.} ② the person who starts a plan or idea {the author of the state reforms}

authority /ɔːˈθɒrəti/ [author n. 创始者，造物者；-ity n.=the quality 表特性→“the quality of an author 创始者的特性”→] n. ① the power you have because of your official position {Only the president has the authority to declare war.} ② an official organization or a government department that has the power to make decisions, and has particular responsibilities {the local authority} ③ someone who knows a lot about a subject and whose knowledge and opinions are greatly respected {Mr Li is a leading authority on Chinese food.}
四级词汇
authorize /ˈɔːθəraɪz/ [author n.创始者（→power权力）；-ize v.=to cause to have 使…有→“to cause to have power 使…有权力”→] v. to give official permission for something {an authorized biography}

blocks.s: 8. bi(o) life 生命，生物

biology /baɪˈɒlədʒi/ [bio=life 生命，生物；-logy n.=branch of science 表学科→] n. ① the scientific study of living things {a degree in biology} ② the scientific laws that control the life of a particular type of animal, plant etc {the biology of bacteria}

biography /baɪˈɒɡrəfi/ [bio=life 生命，生活；-graphy n.=writing 著作→“writing about one's life 关于某个人生平的著作”→] n. a book that tells what has happened in someone’s life, written by someone else {Boswell’s biography of Samuel Johnson}
▽biographer [biograph(y); -er n.] n. 传记作者
biographical [biograph(y); -ical(-al) adj.] adj. 传记（体）的
四级词汇
biochemistry /ˌbaɪəʊˈkeməstri/ [bio-=life 生物；chemistry 化学n.→] n. the scientific study of the chemistry of living things
▽biochemist [bio-; chemist n.] n. 生物化学家

blocks.s: 9. cad, cas, cid to fall or befall 降；降临
四级词汇

case /keɪs/ [cas=to befall 降临；-e→“sth which befalls 降临之事”→] n. ① an example of a particular situation or of something happening {There were 16 cases of damage to cars in the area.} ② a situation that exists, especially as it affects a particular person or group {Changing men’s and women’s traditional roles is not easy, but in our case it has been helpful.}
四级词汇

casual /ˈkæʒuəl/ [cas=to befall 降临；-u-; -al adj.=having the quality 有…性质的→“having the quality of befalling or happening by chance 带有偶发性质的”→] adj. ① happening by chance without being planned {He made some casual remark (=one without thinking much about it) about her holiday.} ② not formal or not for a formal situation {Jean felt more comfortable in casual clothes.}
▽casualty* [casual; -ty n.] n. 事故的伤亡者
四级词汇

occasion /əˈkeɪʒən/ [oc-(ob-)=in the way of 在…面前；cas=to befall 降临；-ion n.=the state or result 表状态或结果→“sth which befalls or happens in one's way 降临在面前或迎面发生的事”→] n. ① a time when something happens; a suitable or favourable time {I’ve seen Jana with them on several occasions.} ② an important social event or ceremony {I’m saving this bottle of champagne for a special occasion.}
▽occasional [occasion; -al adj.] adj. 偶尔的
四级词汇

accident /ˈæksɪdənt/ [ac-(ad-)=towards 朝向；cid=to befall 降临；-ent n.=thing 事→“sth which befalls towards a person 朝着某人降临的事”→] n. ① an event in which a car, train, plane etc is damaged and often someone is hurt {Over 70,000 people are seriously injured every year in road accidents.} ② something that happens without anyone planning or intending it {My third baby was an accident.}
▽accidental [accident; -al a.] a. 意外的；偶然的
四级词汇

incident [in-=on, upon 在…上；cid=to befall 发生；-ent n.=thing 事→“sth which befalls on a particular person or happens at a particular time 发生在某人身上或某个时刻的事”→] n. an event, especially one that is unusual, important, or violent {Roads were sealed off because of a major incident.}
▽incidental [incident; -al a.] a. 偶然的；伴随的
incidence [in-; cid; -ence n.] n. 发生；发生率

The original candy bar industry had its start on the eastern coast in such cities as Philadelphia, Boston, and New York. P1

Mark Twain is one of America's much-beloved authors, creating imaginative and humorous classics for children and adults alike, such as The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, The Prince and The Pauper, and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn. Twain passed away in 1910, leaving behind a treasure of great literature. But now, 100 years after his death, he'll have a brand-new book on the shelves: a three-volume autobiography.
P2
Twain hasn't been keeping busy in his tomb: it was his wish that publishers wait until 100 years after his death to publish his memoirs(自传), which he spent the last decade of his life working on.
P3

The autobiography totals more than 5,000 pages, and likely won't be all sunshine and roses. It seems that Twain harbored some bitterness against former girlfriends and ex-friends. He also writes negatively about politicians of his day, such as Teddy Roosevelt. It's likely that he requested such a long lead time for the memoirs because he didn't want to hurt the feelings of anyone mentioned in this work.
P4

Although small sections of the memoirs have been previously published, the autobiography has never been available in full, and should provide great insights into the man behind the classic books. The first volume of the set will be available in November, and the trilogy is being published by the University of California, Berkeley.
P5

"There are so many biographies of Twain, and many of them have used bits and pieces of the autobiography," editor Robert Hirst told The Independent. "But biographers pick and choose what bits to quote. By publishing Twain's book in full, we hope that people will be able to come to their own complete conclusions about what sort of a man he was."

P1

Sound sleep occurs when one's internal clock is regulated. Circadian rhythms(生理节奏) can become compromised quite easily. Many people with sleep troubles tend to vary bedtimes. To avoid this common problem, sleep sufferers should go to bed and wake up at the same time every day. To help improve circadian rhythms, sufferers should enjoy 15 minutes of sun exposure the first thing in the morning.
P2

A bedtime routine can help prevent insomnia(失眠). One hour before bedtime, one should lower the lights and relax. Reading a book or listening to calm music can help prepare the body for a good night's sleep. Taking a warm, candlelit bath or drinking a cup of warm milk can also help you prepare for deep sleep at night.
P3

Stress can have a bad effect on the body and the ability to sleep. A daily exercise routine can help lower the body's stress naturally. One can also manage stress by writing diaries. Writing diaries can help people express their anxieties, plan for the future and improve sleep. Other ways to lower stress include deep breathing exercises and progressive muscle relaxation.
P4

The light sending out from computers, cellphones, tablets and televisions can cause sleep problems. Therefore, these items should be turned off at least an hour before bedtime. Additionally, lowering the backlight on these electronic devices earlier in the evening can help you fall asleep faster and stay asleep longer once bedtime arrives.

A perfect bedroom invites sweet sleep. Most people sleep better in a cool, dark, and quiet room. Lower the temperature in the room to 16~20 degrees for a peaceful night's sleep. A dark room can be accomplished by installing light blocking curtains or wearing a sleep mask. Noise can be reduced with either earplugs or a white noise machine.
P5 S6
Finally, a comfortable mattress(床垫) and pillows are essential to a good night's sleep.

blocks.s: 2019阅读理解真题2
P1

Tom was aged four but he was talking like a two-year-old baby. He was saying such things as "kick ball" and "want car", and using lots of one-word sentences. He should have been saying some really long sentences and telling stories with them. He wasn't. Something had gone terribly wrong.
P2

Quite a few children have what is called a "language delay". For some reason they don't learn to speak as quickly as they should. Their friends shoot ahead and they're left behind. As a result, they get very lonely. Nobody wants to talk to you if you can't talk back.

Can anything be done to help these children? Yes. They can go to see a speech therapist — a person who's specially trained to work out what's wrong and who knows how to teach language to children. This is what happened to Tom. The speech therapist played some games with him and heard how he talked. She made a recording of his speech, and chatted to his mom and dad about his background.
They'd taken Tom to see doctor, but the doctor hadn't found anything wrong with him. He seemed perfectly normal in every way — except he just wasn't talking.
P4

After Tom and his parents had gone home, the therapist listened carefully to the recording she'd made. Then she looked at a chart which showed how language developed in children aged two, three, and four. She could see Tom was a long way behind.
P5

The next step, she decided, was to teach Tom how to say some new sentences like "kick a red ball," and "the clown is kicking a ball." Tom didn't get the new sentences right straight away. But the therapist was very patient, and after a few more visits he started to make some progress.

B. By sharing experiences of speech therapists.

[P5] The next step, she decided, was to teach Tom how to say some new sentences like "kick a red ball," and "the clown is kicking a ball." Tom didn't get the new sentences right straight away. But the therapist was very patient, and after a few more visits he started to make some progress.

B. What Can Be Done about Kids with Language Delay?

blocks.s: 2019阅读理解真题3
P1

On a dry and cold Friday afternoon last October, Sharon Seline exchanged text messages with her daughter who was in college. They "chatted" back and forth, with the mom asking how things were going and the daughter answering positively followed by emoticons(表情符) showing smiles, b-i-g smiles and hearts.
P2
Later that night, her daughter attempted suicide.
P3

In the days that followed, it came to light that she'd hidden herself in her dorm, crying and showing signs of depression — a completely different reality from the one that she conveyed in texts and Facebook posts.
P4

As human beings, our only real method of connection is through real communication. Studies show that only 7% of communication is based on writing and speaking. The majority of 93% is based on body language. Indeed, it's only when we can hear a tone of voice or look into someone's eyes that we're able to know when "I'm fine" doesn't mean they're fine at all.
P5
This is where social media gets risky.
P6

With modern technology, anyone can hide behind the text, the e-mail, or the Facebook post, projecting any image they want and creating a false image of their choosing. They can be whoever they want to be. And without the ability to receive body language, their audiences are none the wiser.
P7
This presents a paradox which doesn't exist before. With all the powerful social technologies at our fingertips, we are more connected — and potentially more disconnected — than ever before.
P8

Every relevant metric(衡量标准) shows that we are interacting at a great speed and frequency through social media. But are we really communicating? With 93% of our communication context(语境) lost, we are now attempting to establish relationships and make decisions based on phrases or emoticons, which may or may not accurately represent the truth.

D. The users' voices can hardly be heard.

B. People can be both connected and disconnected.
C. People can end up being both wise and stupid.
D. People can form both true and false impressions.
[P7] This presents a paradox which doesn't exist before. With all the powerful social technologies at our fingertips, we are more connected — and potentially more disconnected — than ever before.
What is true about today's communication through social media?
A. It causes more health risks.
B. It gives little communication context.
C. It leads to better relationships.
D. It improves the quality of interaction.

Alan Lakein, a time management expert, thinks that nothing is a total waste of time, including doing nothing at times. If you arrange things so that you find time to relax and "do nothing", you will get more done and have more fun doing it.

One of his clients, a space engineer, didn't know how to "do nothing". Every minute of his leisure time was scheduled with intense activities. He had an outdoor-activities schedule in which he switched from skiing to tennis. His girlfriend kept up with him in these activities, although she would have preferred just to sit by the fire and relax once in a while.

Like too many people, he felt the need to be doing something all the time, for doing nothing seemed a waste of time. His "relaxing by the fire" consisted of playing chess, reading magazines, or checking emails.

For an experiment, Alan asked him to "waste" his time for five minutes during one of their sessions together. What the engineer ended up doing was relaxing, sitting quietly and daydreaming. When he was finally able to admit that emotional reasons caused him to reject relaxing as a waste of time, he began to look more critically at that way of thinking.

Once he knew that relaxing was a good use of time, he became less serious about being busy and started enjoying each activity more. Previously he had been so busy doing that he had no time to have fun at anything. He began to do less and have more fun.

When Alan saw the client about three years later, he still had as busy a schedule as ever, but he was able to balance his activity with relaxing so that he came back to work Monday morning not feeling tired out from a busy weekend but refreshed.

blocks.s: 2019阅读理解真题5
P1

Socrates is often referred to as one of the founders of Western philosophy, and yet he wrote nothing, established no school, and held no particular theories of his own. What he did do, however, was frequently ask the questions that interested him, and in doing so developed a new way of thinking. This method proceeds(展开) as a dialogue between opposing views, and it earned him many enemies in Athens, where he lived.

As a young man, Socrates is believed to have studied natural philosophy, looking at the various explanations of the nature of the universe, but then became involved in the politics of the city-state and concerned with more down-to-earth moral issues, such as the nature of justice.

However, he was not interested in winning arguments, or arguing for the sake of making money. Nor was he seeking answers or explanations. He was simply examining the basis of the concepts we apply to ourselves (such as “good”, “bad”, and “just”), for he believed that understanding what we are is the first task of philosophy.

He was sentenced to death on charges of corrupting the young with bad ideas. But he also had many followers, and among them was Plato, who recorded Socrates' ideas in the written works, called dialogues, in which Socrates sets about examining various ideas.
P5

Socrates' central concern, then, was the examination of life, and it was his cruel questioning of people's most valued beliefs (largely about themselves) that earned him his enemies — but he remained committed to his task until the very end. According to the account of his defense at his trial, Socrates chose death rather than face a life of ignorance: “The life which is unexamined is not worth living.”

B. Socrates tried to find answers to his questions.

In 2011, a dog owner named Robert uploaded a video titled "Guilty!" to YouTube. He had come home finding his two dogs near an empty bag of cat treats. The first dog behaved calmly. But the second dog, Denver, sat shaking in a corner, her eyes looking down, which made Robert believe it was she who had done it. Seeing her "apparent admission of guilt," he yelled at her, "You did this!" Denver beat her tail nervously.
"You know the routine. In the kennel(狗窝)!" Following the command, the dog shut herself in.

The video quickly gathered a flood of comments. For instance, "I ate an extra large pizza," admits a chocolate Lab. Human enthusiasm for guilty dogs seemed growing.

But according to a researcher at Barnard College, what we consider to be a dog's guilty look is no sign of guilt at all. In a 2009 study, the researcher had owners forbid their dogs from eating an attractive treat, and then asked the owners to leave the room. Vegans try to live, as much as possible, in a way that avoids exploiting and being cruel to animals. This means following a plant-based diet. Vegans do not eat animals or animal-based products like meat, fish, seafood, eggs, honey and dairy products such as cheese.
P1 S4
For many vegans, living a committed vegan lifestyle means not wearing clothes made from animal skins and avoiding any products which have been tested on animals.

Vegans argue that suffering is caused in the production of these foods. For example, they say that, on some dairy farms, male calves(小牛) are killed because they are too expensive to keep, and cows are killed when they get older and produce less milk. As for honey, vegans say that bees make honey for bee, not for humans, and that bees' health can suffer when humans take the honey from them.
P2 S4
Vegans believe that the products they use and consume should be free from not just cruelty but any exploitation of animals.

The main reason for going vegan is probably that they believe animals and all other sentient(有感知能力的) beings should have the right to life and freedom. However, there are other reasons. Vegans argue that the production of meat and other animal products is very bad for the environment. They point out that a huge quantity of water is needed to grow grain to feed animals in the meat industry.

The enormous amount of grain which the meat industry needs often leads to forests being cut down and habitats(栖息地) being lost. In contrast, much lower quantities of grain and water are needed to sustain a vegan diet. In addition, many vegans say that all the nutritious elements our bodies need are contained in a carefully planned vegan diet and that this type of diet helps prevent some diseases.

There are many interesting news items in BP's(英国石油公司) annual Energy Outlook just published. But perhaps the most astonishing suggestion in the report is the idea that cutting back on plastic use could make matters worse. This might be what you would expect BP to say. After all, as one of the world's biggest oil companies, it makes a lot of money from selling products in plastic.
P1 S5
But let's look at the thinking behind BP's argument.

If the current opposing idea about the use of plastic continues, there could be a worldwide ban on single-use plastics by 2040. But the document argues that switching plastic for other materials will have a bigger cost in terms of energy and carbon emissions(排放). That sounds like the law of unintended(非故意的) consequences in action.

When plastic bags are measured against paper or cotton substitutes, a BBC analysis found there wasn't a great deal of difference in their environmental impact. Paper bags require fewer reuses to make them more environmentally friendly than single-use plastic bags, which means customers have to replace paper bags more frequently.

Environmentalists, though, are not entirely convinced. They think that BP is stressing the problem of banning plastic for its own interest. "While it's true that it takes less energy to produce and transport plastic than glass, a glass bottle can be reused dozens of times and is recyclable.
P3 S4
Plus, materials like glass when they escape collection don't go on polluting our oceans and rivers for hundreds of years," said Louise Edge, from Greenpeace UK.
P4

Steps to encourage recycling are being taken. The UK, for example, will introduce a new tax on the manufacture and import of plastic packaging in 2022. There are also lots of developments taking place with alternative materials. These may be the final defense against the unintended consequences of plastic bans.

A. BP has earned a lot of money by selling plastic products.
B. Cutting back on plastic use may bring more problems.

D. Cutting back on plastic use may affect product quality.
